results.approach:
M:N green-task scheduler with per-carrier work-stealing deques, modeled on Go's GMP and Tokio's multi-threaded runtime. N carrier OS threads (N = cpu_count, capped at NOVA_WS_MAX_WORKERS=64) each run their own carrier loop (analogous to the current single nova_rt_sched_run). Each carrier has: (1) a thread-local nova_sched_current, (2) a thread-local carrier fiber, (3) a local FIFO deque of runnable tasks, and (4) thread-local io_waiters / sleep_waiters / offload_waiters lists for tasks that PARKED on that carrier. When a carrier's local deque is empty, it steals from a random victim's deque (LIFO steal, FIFO local pop -- the Chase-Lev discipline for cache-warm stealing). A single global mutex-protected overflow queue catches spawns from non-carrier contexts and serves as the "last resort" for stealing when all deques are empty.

Why work-stealing deques over a single global locked run-queue: the single global queue is the bottleneck. With N carriers all doing nova_rq_pop/nova_rq_push under one lock, contention grows linearly with core count. Per-carrier deques mean the LOCAL push/pop path is uncontended (the carrier is the sole owner); only steal touches another carrier's deque, and steal is the COLD path (happens only when idle). Go's runtime and Tokio both validated this: Go uses per-P run-queues with a global fallback; Tokio uses per-worker Chase-Lev deques. The existing code at lines 4593-4807 already defines NovaWSDeque and ws_worker_loop, but that machinery is an INDEPENDENT work-stealing subsystem (exposed as ws_init/ws_spawn/ws_shutdown builtins) that does NOT integrate with the green scheduler's parking, I/O polling, sleep waiters, offload pool, channel green-waiter queues, or nova_sched_current. The M:N design replaces the single-carrier nova_rt_sched_run (line 4501) with N carrier threads each running a carrier_loop that integrates ALL of these subsystems, and repurposes the WS deque primitives (ws_deque_init/push/pop/steal at lines 4629-4697) as the per-carrier run-queue.

Critical constraint: Windows Fibers (CreateFiber/SwitchToFiber) and the POSIX asm context switch (nova_asm_switch at line 3919) are both inherently cross-thread-safe in principle: the saved/restored state is the register set + stack pointer, which is thread-independent. Windows documentation explicitly states "A fiber can be scheduled to run on any thread." The POSIX asm switch saves/restores only callee-saved registers (rbx, rbp, r12-r15) + rsp, which is also thread-independent. So a task parked on carrier-0 CAN be unparked and resumed on carrier-1, provided: (a) the fiber's resumer pointer is updated to the new carrier's carrier_fiber, (b) nova_current_fiber and nova_current_task TLS are repointed on the new carrier. Both already happen in nova_rt_fiber_resume (lines 3860-3875 Win, 3993-4008 POSIX): the resumer is set to the calling carrier's current_fiber, and after the switch, TLS is restored. So migration is FREE -- no special machinery needed.
results.shared_state_plan:
LOCK INVENTORY (ordered by lock-ordering rank, lowest acquired first):

RANK 0 -- Channel locks (ch->lock, per-channel, already exists at line 3304/3308):
  Used by: channel_send, channel_recv, channel_close, channel_try_recv, nova_sched_notify_channel.
  What they protect: ch->buf, ch->count, ch->head, ch->closed, ch->green_waiters, ch->green_send_waiters.
  CHANGE: channel green-waiter wake functions (nova_sched_wake_one at line 4176, nova_sched_wake_send_one at line 4184) currently push directly to the GLOBAL nova_rq_push. In M:N, they push to the CALLER's local deque (the caller holds the channel lock and is running on a known carrier, so `g_carriers[nova_carrier_id].deque` is safe). This is correct because wake_one is always called WHILE HOLDING ch->lock, and the push target is the caller's OWN deque (no cross-carrier deque access needed).

RANK 1 -- Global run-queue lock (NEW: nova_global_rq_lock):
  A single mutex protecting a global overflow FIFO (nova_global_rq_head/tail).
  Used by: (a) nova_rt_sched_spawn when called from a non-carrier thread (e.g., an offload worker or OS-pool thread); (b) global_rq_steal() when a carrier's local deque AND all steal attempts fail; (c) spawn from a carrier pushes to the LOCAL deque first, only overflows to global if the local deque is full (NOVA_WS_DEQUE_CAP=4096 -- unlikely but safe).
  Contention: LOW. The local deque handles 99%+ of pushes; global queue is fallback only.

RANK 2 -- Per-carrier deque lock (already exists in NovaWSDeque at line 4607/4609):
  The existing ws_deque_push/pop/steal use a per-deque mutex. Push and pop are LOCAL-only (the owning carrier); steal is called by OTHER carriers. The mutex serializes steal vs local-pop to prevent the ABA race on the bottom/top indices.
  OPTIMIZATION (Step 3+): Replace the mutex-based deque with a true Chase-Lev lock-free deque (atomic bottom/top with memory ordering). Push/pop become lock-free on the local side; steal uses CAS on top. But the mutex version is correct and sufficient for Step 1-2.

RANK 3 -- Offload pool lock (nova_offload_lock at line 4334/4337, already exists):
  Protects: nova_offload_qhead/qtail (the work queue from green tasks to offload workers).
  NO CHANGE needed. Offload workers dequeue jobs under this lock; green tasks enqueue under this lock. The per-carrier offload_waiters list is carrier-local (only the owning carrier reads/writes it), so no lock needed there.

RANK 4 -- nova_sched_live (atomic counter, replaces the plain int64_t at line 4125):
  Currently `static int64_t nova_sched_live` is read/written without synchronization. In M:N, multiple carriers increment (spawn) and decrement (task finish). CHANGE: make it `volatile int64_t` with `__atomic_fetch_add` / `__atomic_fetch_sub` / `__atomic_load`. No lock needed.

RANK 5 -- nova_mem_lock (line 405/407, already exists):
  Protects the heap allocator. Already thread-safe. No change.

RANK 6 -- nova_strpool_lock (line 303/305), nova_file_mtx (line 9590/9592), g_weak_mtx (line 13172/13174), g_proc_mtx (line 13246/13248):
  All already exist and are thread-safe. No change.

LOCK ORDERING RULE: Never acquire a higher-ranked lock while holding a lower-ranked lock. Specifically:
  - Channel lock (rank 0) never acquires the global RQ lock (rank 1) or a deque lock (rank 2). This is satisfied: wake_one pushes to the LOCAL deque, which acquires the deque lock (rank 2). But wait -- that violates rank 0 < rank 2. RESOLUTION: wake_one's push to the local deque is safe because it's the CALLER's own deque, and no other lock acquisition happens inside ws_deque_push. The risk is if a carrier holds deque lock and then tries to acquire a channel lock -- this DOES happen (the carrier pops a task, runs it, task does channel_send which acquires ch->lock). But that's deque-lock RELEASED before ch->lock acquired (pop releases the deque lock, then the task code runs and acquires ch->lock). So there is no nested holding. The actual concern is wake_one: it's called with ch->lock HELD, and it calls ws_deque_push which acquires deque lock. So the nesting is ch->lock -> deque lock. This is safe as long as we never do deque lock -> ch->lock. And we don't: the carrier loop does ws_deque_pop (acquires/releases deque lock), THEN runs the task (which may acquire ch->lock). Sequential, not nested.

I/O WAITERS (nova_io_waiters, currently global at line 4126):
  Becomes per-carrier: each NovaCarrier has its own io_waiters list. When a green task calls nova_sched_park_io (line 4199), it registers on g_carriers[nova_carrier_id].io_waiters. The carrier loop calls nova_carrier_poll_io which scans ONLY its own list. NO LOCK needed (single-writer: the carrier thread itself, since the parked task was running ON this carrier when it parked, and the carrier scans its own list).

SLEEP WAITERS (nova_sleep_waiters, currently global at line 4127):
  Same pattern: per-carrier. nova_sched_park_sleep (line 4252) registers on g_carriers[nova_carrier_id].sleep_waiters. Carrier loop scans its own list. No lock needed.

OFFLOAD WAITERS (nova_offload_waiters, currently global at line 4331):
  Same pattern: per-carrier. nova_offload_run (line 4391) registers on g_carriers[nova_carrier_id].offload_waiters before yielding. The carrier loop scans its own list via nova_sched_check_offload. The offload WORKER sets `job->done` with RELEASE semantics (line 4362, already atomic); the carrier reads with ACQUIRE (line 4428, already atomic). No lock needed for the waiter list itself. This is the "F1 race" discipline already proven: the offload worker never touches the waiter list or the run queue; it only sets the done flag. The carrier is the sole entity that reads the waiter list and re-enqueues.

CHANNEL GREEN-WAITER QUEUES (ch->green_waiters, ch->green_send_waiters):
  These are per-channel, protected by ch->lock. The critical M:N change: when carrier-A's task parks on a channel (nova_sched_park_on, line 4142), it links itself onto ch->green_waiters under ch->lock. Later, carrier-B's task sends on the same channel (nova_sched_wake_one, line 4176) under ch->lock, pops the waiter, and pushes it to carrier-B's LOCAL deque. The parked task now migrates from carrier-A to carrier-B. This is correct because: (a) the task is not on any carrier's structures (it parked, so it's not in any deque or waiter list except ch->green_waiters); (b) the fiber resume will happen on carrier-B (carrier-B will pop it from its deque and call nova_rt_fiber_resume, which repoints resumer/TLS). No additional synchronization needed beyond ch->lock.
results.channel_plan:
CURRENT STATE: Channel operations (send/recv/close/select) already acquire ch->lock (per-channel mutex) before touching the buffer or green-waiter lists. The green park/unpark functions (nova_sched_park_on at line 4142, nova_sched_wake_one at line 4176) are called WHILE HOLDING ch->lock. This is already correct for M:N because:

1. PARK (receiver on carrier-A finds empty channel):
   - Acquires ch->lock
   - Calls nova_sched_park_on: sets task->status=2, links task onto ch->green_waiters
   - Releases ch->lock
   - Calls nova_sched_yield_now (nova_rt_fiber_yield): switches back to carrier-A's carrier_fiber
   - Carrier-A's loop sees the task is not on its deque (task self-removed before parking)
   - SAFE: the task is now ONLY on ch->green_waiters, protected by ch->lock

2. UNPARK (sender on carrier-B sends a value):
   - Acquires ch->lock
   - Enqueues value into ch->buf
   - Calls nova_sched_wake_one: pops task from ch->green_waiters, sets task->status=0, pushes to carrier-B's LOCAL deque (ws_deque_push(&g_carriers[nova_carrier_id].deque, task))
   - Releases ch->lock
   - SAFE: the task is now on carrier-B's deque, will be resumed by carrier-B
   - MIGRATION happened: task was parked by carrier-A, will run on carrier-B. Fiber resume handles TLS repointing.

3. LOST-WAKEUP PREVENTION:
   The current code has a subtle race in the green path: after nova_sched_park_on links the task, but before nova_sched_yield_now executes, could another carrier send on the channel and wake the task? YES -- but this is safe. The wake sets task->status=0 and pushes to the waker's deque. Then the original carrier calls nova_rt_fiber_yield. But wait -- the task is now on TWO places: the waker's deque AND about to yield. The yield switches to the carrier fiber, and the carrier loop's next iteration will NOT see this task (it was not pushed to the local deque by park_on -- park_on only sets status=2 and links to green_waiters). But the waker already REMOVED it from green_waiters and put it on the waker's deque with status=0. So when the original carrier's fiber_yield returns control to the carrier loop, the carrier loop just continues to the next iteration. The waker's carrier will eventually pop the task and resume it. The fiber_resume will find the task in status=0 (runnable), set it to 1 (running), and proceed.

   ACTUALLY, there is a real race here that must be addressed: between the park_on (which links the task to green_waiters under ch->lock) and the yield_now (which is called AFTER releasing ch->lock), the task is in a liminal state: it's on green_waiters, its status is 2 (parked), but it hasn't actually context-switched yet. If another carrier wakes it during this window, the waker calls ws_deque_push on its own deque. Then the waker's carrier might pop and resume the task BEFORE the original carrier has finished yielding. This would mean TWO carriers are trying to run the same fiber simultaneously -- a catastrophic race.

   FIX: The park_on + yield_now sequence must be ATOMIC with respect to the channel lock. Looking at the current code (lines 3393-3422 for send, 3497-3513 for recv): park_on is called WHILE holding ch->lock, yield_now is called AFTER releasing ch->lock. This is the F1 race in its exact form.

   RESOLUTION for M:N: Change nova_sched_park_on to NOT link the task onto green_waiters. Instead, the channel_send/recv green path should: (a) under ch->lock, link task onto green_waiters; (b) STILL UNDER ch->lock, set task->status = 2; (c) release ch->lock; (d) call yield_now. The waker that finds the task on green_waiters with status=2 will dequeue it and push to its deque. But can the waker's carrier resume it before the parker yields? NO -- because the parker is still RUNNING on its carrier. The parker's carrier will not pop anything new until the parker yields. The waker pushes the task to the WAKER's deque. The waker's carrier might try to pop and resume it. The fiber_resume call on the waker's carrier will call SwitchToFiber/nova_asm_switch, which will block until... wait, no. SwitchToFiber doesn't block -- it immediately starts running the fiber's saved context. If the fiber hasn't yielded yet (it's still running on carrier-A), then carrier-B calling SwitchToFiber on it is UNDEFINED BEHAVIOR (two threads running the same stack).

   CORRECT FIX: The task must NOT be visible to any waker until it has ACTUALLY yielded. The solution (used by Go and Tokio): the park operation must be done in two phases:
   Phase 1 (under ch->lock): Set a "will park" flag but do NOT put the task on green_waiters yet. Instead, put a WAITER RECORD (not the task itself) that contains a pointer to the task and an atomic "parked" flag set to 0.
   Phase 2 (after releasing ch->lock): Call yield_now. On yield, the carrier loop sets the waiter's "parked" flag to 1 atomically.
   Waker: Under ch->lock, finds the waiter. Checks "parked" flag. If 1, safe to dequeue and push to deque. If 0, the task hasn't yielded yet -- set a "wake pending" flag. When the task finally yields, the carrier checks "wake pending" and immediately re-enqueues.

   SIMPLER CORRECT FIX (recommended, matches Go): Do the green_waiters linkage AND the yield WHILE still holding ch->lock. The yield switches to the carrier fiber; the carrier fiber runs the carrier loop which will NOT acquire ch->lock (it just pops from its deque). So holding ch->lock across the yield is safe -- no deadlock risk because the carrier loop does not acquire channel locks. The waker on another carrier acquires ch->lock, finds the task, wakes it. By the time the waker acquires ch->lock, the parker has already yielded (it's sitting in the carrier fiber's context switch). This is correct. COST: the channel lock is held during the context switch (~50ns), slightly increasing contention on that specific channel. Acceptable.

   IMPLEMENTATION: In nova_rt_channel_recv's green path (lines 3497-3513), change to:
   ```
   // under ch->lock:
   nova_sched_park_on(ch);         // link to green_waiters, set status=2
   // DO NOT release ch->lock yet
   nova_sched_yield_now();         // context-switch to carrier (carrier loop runs)
   // when resumed, we're back here. Release ch->lock:
   unlock(ch->lock);
   // retry the recv
   ```
   Wait -- this won't work because the carrier loop needs to not hold any locks. Actually it DOES work: yield_now switches to the carrier fiber. The carrier fiber is in the carrier loop, which was in the middle of nova_rt_fiber_resume. After resume returns, the carrier loop continues. ch->lock is held on the TASK's stack frame -- the carrier thread's execution is now in the carrier loop (different stack), so ch->lock is "held" by a suspended stack frame that will only execute again when the task is resumed. On POSIX mutexes, this is fine because mutex ownership is per-thread, and the carrier thread no longer considers itself the lock holder (it returned from fiber_resume). WRONG -- POSIX mutexes track the calling thread, and the carrier thread IS the thread that locked it. The carrier thread would deadlock if it tried to lock the same channel's lock again.

   CORRECT FINAL APPROACH: Use a per-task atomic flag. Before releasing ch->lock, set task->park_complete = 0. Release ch->lock. Yield. The carrier, after fiber_resume returns, atomically sets task->park_complete = 1 for the just-yielded task. The waker, after removing the task from green_waiters (under ch->lock), spins briefly on task->park_complete before pushing to its deque. Spin is bounded: the parker is in the process of yielding (a few instructions of context-switch), so park_complete becomes 1 within ~100ns. This is the approach Tokio uses for its waker safety.

   EVEN SIMPLER: Keep the current code structure (park under lock, release lock, yield). Add a field to NovaSchedTask: `volatile int park_committed;`. Set it to 0 in park_on. In the carrier loop, after fiber_resume returns and the task's status is 2 (parked), set task->park_committed = 1 with RELEASE semantics. In wake_one, after dequeuing from green_waiters, spin-wait on park_committed with ACQUIRE semantics before pushing to the deque. The spin is bounded (< 200ns, just the context-switch latency).

VALIDATION: run green_scale_test (10k tasks) -- it must complete with 2 carriers; verify tasks actually ran on 2 OS threads (add a thread-id stamp to each task on completion, check that at least 2 distinct thread IDs appear). This step is CORRECT but SLOW (global lock contention). That's fine -- correctness first.

STEP 2 â€” Per-carrier waiter lists (io, sleep, offload). CHANGES: (a) define NovaCarrier struct with io_waiters, sleep_waiters, offload_waiters fields; (b) nova_sched_park_io/park_sleep/offload_run register on g_carriers[nova_carrier_id].X instead of globals; (c) carrier loop calls nova_carrier_wake_sleepers/poll_io/check_offload on its own NovaCarrier; (d) these per-carrier lists need NO lock (single-writer: the carrier thread). (e) The global run-queue lock still protects rq_push/rq_pop. VALIDATION: run green_netpoll_test (echo server with concurrent accepts + I/O parking); run the DNS offload test (dns_resolve_all). Both must pass. Add a test that spawns tasks doing sleep() on different carriers and verify they wake at the right time.

STEP 3 â€” Per-carrier deques + work-stealing (PERFORMANCE). CHANGES: (a) each NovaCarrier gets a NovaWSDeque (reuse the existing ws_deque_init/push/pop/steal at lines 4629-4697); (b) nova_rt_sched_spawn pushes to the spawning carrier's local deque (if on a carrier) or to the global overflow queue (if not); (c) carrier loop: pop from local deque first, then try global_rq_steal, then steal from random victim; (d) wake_one/wake_send_one/wake_all push to the waking carrier's local deque; (e) yield_runnable pushes to local deque; (f) make g_ws_rng_state per-carrier (thread-local). VALIDATION: run green_scale_test with N=cpu_count carriers. Measure throughput vs Step 1 (should be 2-4x on 4+ cores due to reduced contention). Verify work-stealing actually occurs: add a counter per carrier of tasks stolen, check it's > 0 in a test that spawns tasks on one carrier and has others idle.

STEP 4 â€” Carrier count = cpu_count, NOVA_CARRIERS env var, cleanup. Measure wake latency (should be < 10us on modern OS).
risks: RISK 1 â€” F1 RACE (park/wake overlap): A task parks on a channel (links to green_waiters, sets status=2) then releases ch->lock then yields. Between lock-release and yield, another carrier can wake the task and try to resume it while the original carrier hasn't finished the context switch. MITIGATION: park_committed atomic flag + spin-wait in wake_one (bounded ~100ns). This is the HIGHEST priority correctness concern. The existing single-carrier code is immune because there is only one carrier, so wake_one's push just puts the task in the run queue and the carrier will get to it after finishing the current yield. In M:N, a DIFFERENT carrier can grab it immediately. The spin-wait on park_committed is the standard solution (Tokio uses an equivalent 'notified' state machine).

RISK 2 â€” Windows Fiber cross-thread safety: While Microsoft documents 'A fiber can be scheduled to run on any thread', some older MSDN articles and Raymond Chen blog posts note that fibers interacting with certain CRT functions (thread-local destructors, SEH chain) can behave unexpectedly across threads. MITIGATION: (a) NOVA fibers already use a VEH (vectored exception handler, line 3806) instead of SEH, which is process-wide and thread-safe; (b) each fiber entry (nova_fiber_entry, line 3826) sets nova_current_fiber and nova_current_task, so TLS is correctly repointed; (c) test cross-thread fiber migration explicitly in Step 1 (spawn a task on carrier-0, park it, wake it on carrier-1, verify it runs correctly).

RISK 3 â€” Starvation of per-carrier waiter lists: I/O waiters, sleep waiters, and offload waiters are per-carrier. If a task parks on I/O on carrier-0, and carrier-0 is busy running CPU-bound tasks, the I/O waiter won't be polled until carrier-0's next idle moment. MITIGATION: (a) the carrier loop polls waiters on EVERY iteration, not just when idle (same as current code at lines 4504-4519); (b) cooperative yield (reschedule()) already exists for CPU-bound tasks; (c) post-v1: involuntary preemption (signal-based) would force yields. This is a known limitation of cooperative scheduling, not new to M:N.

RISK 4 â€” Global run-queue as bottleneck in Step 1: With a single global lock around all rq/waiter operations, Step 1 will have HIGH contention with many carriers. This is by design (correctness first), but if Step 1 is SLOWER than single-carrier for some workloads, it could be confusing. MITIGATION: Step 1 uses only 2 carriers (hardcoded) where contention is minimal. Step 3 eliminates the bottleneck with per-carrier deques.

RISK 5 â€” select() green path busy-loops across carriers: The current select() (line 3650) does yield_runnable in a loop, trying each channel. In M:N, this means a select-ing task bounces between carriers (yield pushes to local deque, carrier pops it, it tries channels, yields again). This wastes CPU. MITIGATION: defer to post-M:N. A proper multi-channel park (park on ALL channels simultaneously, wake on first ready) is a separate feature. The current busy-yield is correct, just not optimal.

RISK 6 â€” ws_deque overflow: The deque is fixed at NOVA_WS_DEQUE_CAP=4096. If a carrier has >4096 runnable tasks, ws_deque_push silently overwrites (the current code at line 4647 does `d->buf[b % NOVA_WS_DEQUE_CAP] = t` without checking capacity). MITIGATION: (a) add a capacity check to ws_deque_push; if full, push to the global overflow queue instead; (b) 4096 is generous â€” a carrier with that many runnable tasks is unusual; (c) the global overflow queue acts as unbounded spillover.

RISK 7 â€” nova_sched_notify_channel (line 4461) is called from the carrier loop AFTER a task completes (to notify monitors). It acquires ch->lock and calls wake_one, which pushes to the carrier's local deque. This is correct but note: if the completed task was the ROOT task and the carrier is about to shut down, the woken monitor-waiter must still be processed. MITIGATION: the carrier loop continues after task completion (it doesn't exit immediately on root completion â€” it loops until nova_sched_live == 0). So monitor notifications are processed.

RISK 8 â€” Thread-safety of nova_current_task (line 70/73): Already __thread/__declspec(thread), so already safe for M:N. But nova_fiber_entry (line 3826-3829) and nova_posix_fiber_trampoline (line 3940-3941) set nova_current_task = &f->task on fiber entry. In M:N, this happens on whichever carrier resumes the fiber â€” correct because the fiber runs on that carrier's thread. No risk here, just confirming.

RISK 9 â€” The existing standalone ws_worker_loop (line 4713) calls nova_rt_fiber_resume directly from its worker thread, but does NOT call nova_ensure_carrier first (the carrier loop at line 4526 does: the fiber_resume function itself calls nova_ensure_carrier at line 3863/3996). This means each WS worker thread gets converted to a fiber on first resume. In M:N, each carrier thread similarly calls nova_ensure_carrier. The risk is: if the standalone WS API and the new carrier system are both active, ConvertThreadToFiber might be called twice on the same thread. MITIGATION: nova_ensure_carrier already checks nova_carrier_ready (line 3785) and is idempotent. But the standalone WS API should be deprecated or merged.

races.scenario: RACE 1: nova_sched_current is a plain static global (line 4123: `static NovaSchedTask* nova_sched_current = NULL`), not __thread. Every carrier OS thread would read/write it concurrently. Carrier A sets it at line 4524 (`nova_sched_current = t`), runs the fiber, then clears it at line 4527 (`nova_sched_current = NULL`). Meanwhile carrier B does the same. The running green task calls nova_sched_park_on (line 4143: `NovaSchedTask* t = nova_sched_current`) or nova_sched_park_sleep (line 4253) or nova_offload_run (line 4394: `job->task = nova_sched_current`) and reads a STALE or WRONG pointer -- it gets carrier B's task instead of its own, or NULL.
races.why: With N carriers, nova_sched_current is a shared non-atomic global written by all carriers and read by every green task. There is no lock, no TLS, no atomic. This is a textbook data race (C11 UB). Every scheduler operation that touches nova_sched_current -- park, yield, offload, sleep -- will malfunction: tasks park the WRONG task, offload jobs record the wrong task pointer, yield re-enqueues the wrong task. A single write from another carrier corrupts the identity of every running task.
races.fix: Make nova_sched_current __thread (__declspec(thread) on Windows). Each carrier sets its own TLS copy before resuming a fiber and clears it after. Green tasks read only their carrier's copy.

races.scenario: RACE 2: The global run queue (nova_rq_head/nova_rq_tail, lines 4121-4122) is an intrusive linked list with zero synchronization. nova_rq_push (line 4129) and nova_rq_pop (line 4134) are called by: the carrier loop (line 4505/4520), nova_sched_wake_one (line 4182), nova_sched_wake_send_one (line 4190), nova_sched_yield_runnable (line 4158), nova_sched_wake_sleepers (line 4242), nova_sched_poll_io (line 4302), nova_sched_check_offload (line 4431), and nova_rt_sched_spawn (line 4490). With M carriers, ALL of these execute concurrently on different OS threads.
races.why: Two carriers calling nova_rq_push simultaneously corrupt the linked list: both read nova_rq_tail, both write t->next=NULL, one's write to nova_rq_tail overwrites the other's, and a task is lost (leaked) or the list is corrupted (dangling pointer). Similarly, two concurrent nova_rq_pop calls can return the same task to two carriers, causing double-resume (fiber corruption). This is not just a data race; it is structural corruption of the scheduler's primary data structure.
races.fix: Either (a) replace the global run queue with per-carrier local deques + a work-stealing protocol (the ws_deque already exists at line 4599 but is disconnected from the main scheduler), or (b) protect nova_rq_push/pop with a global spinlock/mutex. Option (a) is required for scalability.

races.scenario: RACE 3: nova_io_waiters (line 4126) and nova_sleep_waiters (line 4127) are global unsynchronized intrusive linked lists. nova_sched_park_io (line 4199) pushes to nova_io_waiters from a green task (running on carrier A). nova_sched_poll_io (line 4270) iterates and mutates the list (splicing out ready waiters) from the carrier loop. nova_sched_wake_sleepers (line 4232) does the same for sleep waiters. With M carriers, task X on carrier A parks on I/O, while carrier B is iterating nova_io_waiters in poll_io. The concurrent list mutation corrupts the linked list.
races.why: park_io does `w->next = nova_io_waiters; nova_io_waiters = w;` (lines 4207-4208) -- a non-atomic linked-list prepend. If carrier B is simultaneously in nova_sched_poll_io traversing the list with `pp = &nova_io_waiters; while (*pp)` (line 4293), the prepend can make B skip the new waiter or follow a stale ->next. Worse, poll_io splices out nodes (`*pp = w->next`, line 4300) while another carrier is prepending, causing a lost waiter (task never wakes, permanent deadlock for that task). Same problem for sleep_waiters.
races.fix: Centralize I/O and sleep waiters on a single dedicated netpoller thread, or protect each waiter list with a mutex. Alternatively, make waiter lists per-carrier (each carrier polls only its own waiters) and ensure park_io always adds to the local carrier's list.

races.scenario: RACE 4: nova_offload_waiters (line 4331, declared `carrier-local`) is a global static pointer, not TLS. nova_offload_run (line 4391) does `job->wnext = nova_offload_waiters; nova_offload_waiters = job` (lines 4399-4400) from the green task (which runs on a carrier). nova_sched_check_offload (line 4423) iterates and splices this list from the carrier loop. With M carriers, carrier A's green task adds to the list while carrier B scans it -- classic linked-list race.
races.why: The comment at line 4331 says 'carrier-local' but it is actually `static NovaOffloadJob* nova_offload_waiters = NULL` -- a plain global, not __thread. The F1 discipline (offload worker never resumes a fiber, only the carrier does) was designed for ONE carrier. With M carriers, the invariant 'only one thread touches nova_offload_waiters' is violated. Two carriers concurrently inserting/scanning corrupt the waiter list, causing tasks to never be re-enqueued (lost wakeup / permanent hang).
races.fix: Make nova_offload_waiters __thread (per-carrier) so each carrier only scans its own offload waiters. The offload worker's __atomic_store_n(&job->done, 1, RELEASE) is already carrier-agnostic -- each carrier scans its own jobs.

races.scenario: RACE 5: Channel green_waiters and green_send_waiters (lines 3301-3302) are manipulated by nova_sched_park_on (line 4142), nova_sched_park_send (line 4149), nova_sched_wake_one (line 4176), and nova_sched_wake_send_one (line 4184). These park/wake functions are called INSIDE the channel lock. BUT nova_sched_wake_one calls nova_rq_push (line 4182) -- which modifies the global run queue while still inside the channel lock. With M carriers, carrier A wakes a task on carrier B's behalf by pushing it onto the global run queue. Carrier B then pops and resumes it. This creates a cross-carrier fiber resume.
races.why: The channel lock protects the waiter list manipulation itself, but the CONSEQUENCE is that a task parked on carrier A (its fiber's resumer points to carrier A's carrier_fiber) gets pushed to the global run queue and popped by carrier B. Carrier B calls nova_rt_fiber_resume, which does SwitchToFiber (Win, line 3868) or nova_asm_switch (POSIX, line 4002) into a fiber whose resumer is carrier A's carrier_fiber. When the fiber yields, it SwitchToFiber(me->resumer->handle) (line 3881/4016) -- switching to carrier A's fiber FROM carrier B's OS thread. On Windows, SwitchToFiber across OS threads is UNDEFINED BEHAVIOR (fibers are thread-affine). On POSIX, the asm switch restores a stack pointer belonging to carrier A's thread -- stack corruption.
races.fix: Fibers must be thread-affine: a task that was last suspended on carrier A must only be resumed on carrier A. Either (a) each task records its home carrier and the wake path sends it to that carrier's local queue (not a global queue), or (b) on resume, detach the old resumer and set resumer to the current carrier's carrier_fiber. Option (b) is what Go does (goroutines have no thread affinity). The resumer field must be set to the RESUMING carrier's carrier_fiber, not preserved from the original.

races.scenario: RACE 6: nova_sched_live (line 4125: `static int64_t nova_sched_live = 0`) is incremented by nova_rt_sched_spawn (line 4491: `nova_sched_live++`) and decremented by the carrier loop on task completion (line 4552: `nova_sched_live--`). These are non-atomic read-modify-write operations on a shared counter. With M carriers, concurrent increment/decrement is a data race.
races.why: nova_sched_live controls the carrier loop termination condition (line 4503: `while (nova_sched_live > 0)`). A torn read/write means the scheduler can terminate prematurely (live count goes to 0 when tasks are still running) or never terminate (live count never reaches 0). On x86 the ++ is likely a single instruction but the C standard does not guarantee this; on ARM it is definitely not atomic.
races.fix: Make nova_sched_live an atomic int64_t and use atomic increment/decrement. Similarly for nova_sched_running (line 4124).

races.scenario: RACE 7: nova_is_multithreaded (line 400: `static volatile int nova_is_multithreaded = 0`) is only set to 1 in the OS-pool spawn path (line 5307). In green-mode (nova_green_enabled()==1 && nova_sched_running==1), spawn routes to nova_rt_sched_spawn (line 5304-5305), which NEVER sets nova_is_multithreaded. So with M carrier OS threads running green tasks concurrently, nova_is_multithreaded remains 0.
races.why: When nova_is_multithreaded==0, nova_rc_inc (line 6853-6861) uses non-atomic `NOVA_RC_COUNT(ptr)++` instead of InterlockedIncrement. With M carriers, two green tasks on different OS threads can inc/dec the same RC simultaneously (e.g., both received a deep_copy of a string that shares the same interned pointer, or a channel shared between tasks). The non-atomic RC update causes use-after-free (RC goes to 0 too early) or memory leak (RC never reaches 0). This is silent heap corruption.
races.fix: Set nova_is_multithreaded=1 when M>1 carriers are started, BEFORE any carrier thread begins executing. Alternatively, always use atomic RC ops when the green scheduler is active with multiple carriers.

races.scenario: RACE 8: The string intern table (nova_intern_table, lines 647-650) is a global hash table with zero synchronization. nova_intern_h (line 685) reads and writes nova_intern_table, nova_intern_hashes, nova_intern_cap, nova_intern_used. With M carriers, two green tasks interning strings concurrently will corrupt the table -- especially during nova_intern_grow (line 661) which reallocates and rehashes.
races.why: String interning is called on every string comparison, format, and dict operation. Two concurrent calls to nova_intern_h can both decide to grow the table, leading to double-free of the old table, or one thread reads from a table that the other just freed. Even without growth, concurrent insertion into the open-addressing table causes lost entries (two threads pick the same slot). This is heap corruption + data loss.
races.fix: Protect the intern table with a mutex, or use a concurrent hash map, or make the intern table per-carrier (with a shared read-only global table for compile-time constants).

races.scenario: RACE 9: nova_heap_alloc (line 429) updates nova_mem_total++ and nova_mem_live++ (lines 444-445) non-atomically. nova_track_heap_bounds (line 175) updates nova_heap_base and nova_heap_top with non-atomic compare-and-store. With M carriers allocating concurrently, these are data races.
races.why: nova_mem_live is used for diagnostics (nova_rt_live_count, line 6902) so the race 'only' causes wrong counts. But nova_heap_base/nova_heap_top are used by nova_mem_find_tag (line 512) and nova_rc_is_managed (line 6838) to REJECT non-pointer values before dereferencing. A torn write to nova_heap_top (e.g., a half-updated 64-bit value on a 32-bit system, or a reordered store) could cause nova_rc_is_managed to dereference a non-pointer, crashing or corrupting memory. On 64-bit x86 the store is naturally atomic, but on ARM/32-bit it is not.
races.fix: Use atomic stores for nova_heap_base/nova_heap_top (at minimum release/acquire). Make nova_mem_total/nova_mem_live atomic.

races.scenario: RACE 10: The box tracking range (g_box_lo/g_box_hi, lines 533-534) is updated by nova_box_track (line 536) with non-atomic compare-and-store. nova_is_box (line 559/561) reads g_box_lo/g_box_hi to reject non-box values. With M carriers, two concurrent nova_rt_box_float calls can race on g_box_lo/g_box_hi, and a concurrent nova_is_box read can see a partially updated range.
races.why: Same class as the heap_base/heap_top race. If g_box_hi is updated but g_box_lo is not yet, nova_is_box could accept a value that is NOT a box, then dereference it as a NovaBox struct -- reading garbage kind/payload fields. This causes wrong program behavior (incorrect type dispatch) or a crash.
races.fix: Use atomic stores (release) in nova_box_track and atomic loads (acquire) in nova_is_box.

races.scenario: RACE 11: g_ws_rng_state (line 4699: `static unsigned int g_ws_rng_state = 1`) is a GLOBAL, not per-worker. ws_random_victim (line 4700) reads and writes it: `g_ws_rng_state = g_ws_rng_state * 1103515245 + 12345`. With M ws_worker_loop threads calling this concurrently, the RNG state is corrupted.
races.why: This is not a safety issue (the worst case is poor randomness leading to all workers stealing from the same victim, causing contention and unfairness) but it IS a C11 data race (undefined behavior). In practice, on x86, the torn read/write causes biased victim selection, degrading work-stealing to ~O(N) contention on one deque instead of O(1) amortized.
races.fix: Make g_ws_rng_state per-worker (store it in NovaWSWorker struct, seed with worker ID).

races.scenario: RACE 12 (LOST-WAKEUP): A sender on carrier A calls nova_sched_wake_one (line 4176) inside the channel lock, which calls nova_rq_push (line 4182) to put the woken task on the global run queue. Carrier B is idle, spinning in its poll loop, and NEVER checks the global run queue -- it only checks its own ws_deque. The woken task sits in the global run queue until carrier A happens to pop it.
races.why: The current architecture has TWO separate scheduling mechanisms: the original single-carrier run queue (nova_rq_head/tail) and the ws_deque system. Channel wake operations push to nova_rq_push but the ws_worker_loop (line 4713) only calls ws_deque_pop/ws_deque_steal. If M:N is built by replacing nova_rt_sched_run with ws_worker_loop, but channel/io/sleep/offload wake paths still call nova_rq_push, woken tasks are LOST (never scheduled). If instead the old run queue is kept alongside ws_deques, there is no mechanism for idle carriers to notice new entries in the global queue.
races.fix: Unify the scheduling: all wake paths must push to the waking carrier's local deque (or a shared injection queue that all carriers poll). Remove the dual-queue architecture entirely.

races.scenario: RACE 13 (DEADLOCK): The carrier loop (nova_rt_sched_run, line 4501) blocks in nova_sched_poll_io with a 10ms timeout (line 4510) when there are I/O waiters but no runnable tasks. With M carriers, ALL carriers could block in select() simultaneously. If a new task is spawned (nova_rt_sched_spawn -> nova_rq_push) while all carriers are blocked in select(), the task waits up to 10ms before any carrier wakes up and runs it. If the spawn happens from an offload worker thread (not a carrier), there is no mechanism to wake any carrier at all -- the offload worker only sets job->done=1.
races.why: There is no cross-carrier signaling mechanism (no eventfd, no pipe, no condition variable to wake idle carriers). When all carriers are blocked in select() or Sleep(1), new work can be stranded for up to 10ms. For offload completions, the comment at line 4420-4422 says 'Runs ONLY on the carrier thread' -- but with M carriers and all of them in select(), no carrier is scanning nova_sched_check_offload. The offload-completed task hangs until a carrier finishes its select timeout.
races.fix: Add a self-pipe or eventfd per carrier. When a task is made runnable (from any context -- wake, spawn, offload completion), write a byte to the target carrier's wakeup FD, which is included in the carrier's select() fd_set. This guarantees O(1) wakeup latency.

races.scenario: RACE 14: Windows SwitchToFiber is THREAD-AFFINE. A fiber created on thread A (via CreateFiber called from carrier A at line 3855) can only be SwitchToFiber'd from thread A. If carrier B (a different OS thread) steals a task and calls SwitchToFiber(f->handle) at line 3868, the behavior is undefined. Microsoft documentation: 'You can call SwitchToFiber with the address of a fiber created by a different thread. To do this, [...] the other fiber must have been created with a call to ConvertThreadToFiber.' But the green task fibers are created with CreateFiber, not ConvertThreadToFiber.
races.why: Windows fibers store thread-local state including the TEB (Thread Environment Block) pointer, structured exception handling chain, and fiber-local storage. SwitchToFiber on a different thread than the one that last ran the fiber corrupts the TEB, causing subsequent Win32 API calls (GetLastError, TLS, exception handling) to reference the wrong thread's state. This is silent corruption that manifests as random crashes, wrong error codes, or security violations.
races.fix: On Windows, either (a) ensure fiber affinity (a fiber only runs on the OS thread that created it -- migration requires destroying and recreating the fiber on the new thread), or (b) abandon Windows Fibers entirely and use the POSIX-style asm context switch (save/restore only callee-saved registers + RSP, which is thread-agnostic). Option (b) is what Go does on Windows (it does not use Windows Fibers).

races.scenario: RACE 15: The slab allocator (nova_slab_alloc, line 238) IS protected by a per-pool lock (lines 240-243). BUT nova_heap_alloc (line 429) calls nova_slab_alloc only for lists and dicts; for all other objects it calls calloc directly (line 438) then nova_track_heap_bounds (non-atomic, see Race 9). The slab allocator itself is safe, but the fallback malloc path has non-atomic nova_mem_total++/nova_mem_live++ at lines 444-445, which is a data race under M carriers.
races.why: Every allocation of a non-list, non-dict object (strings, structs, channels, boxes) goes through the unprotected calloc path. The nova_mem_total/nova_mem_live counters will be incorrect, but more critically, the nova_track_heap_bounds call (line 439) racing with other allocations can produce a temporarily NARROWER range than the actual heap extent, causing nova_rc_is_managed to reject a valid pointer and skip its RC decrement -- memory leak, or worse, skip RC increment -- use-after-free.
races.fix: Protect nova_track_heap_bounds with an atomic CAS loop (compare-and-swap to widen the range). Make nova_mem_total/nova_mem_live atomic.

races.scenario: RACE 16: nova_slab_init (line 211) has a TOCTOU check: `if (nova_slab_inited) return;` followed by init work and `nova_slab_inited = 1`. If two carriers start simultaneously and both call nova_heap_alloc before either completes nova_slab_init, the slab pools get double-initialized -- the second init overwrites the first's pages pointer, leaking memory and corrupting the free list.
races.why: The nova_slab_inited flag is a plain int, not atomic, and the check+set is not atomic. Similarly, nova_offload_ensure (line 4369) has `if (nova_offload_started) return; nova_offload_started = 1;` -- two carriers can both start the offload pool, creating 8 worker threads instead of 4 and double-initializing the lock on Windows.
races.fix: Use a once-init pattern: pthread_once on POSIX, InitOnceExecuteOnce on Windows, or an atomic flag with CAS.

races.scenario: RACE 17: The fault boundary (longjmp in nova_panic, line 134) relies on nova_cur() returning the CURRENT green task's NovaTaskState. nova_cur() (line 76) reads nova_current_task (which IS __thread, line 70/73). When a fiber is resumed on a different carrier (due to work stealing), nova_current_task is set in the fiber entry/resume path (line 3829/3870/3941/4004). But if the fiber crashes BEFORE nova_current_task is set (e.g., during the SwitchToFiber itself, or in the first instruction of the fiber trampoline), nova_cur() returns the carrier's default TLS state, and longjmp goes to the CARRIER's jmp_buf -- crashing the carrier instead of containing the fault.
races.why: The window between SwitchToFiber (line 3868) and the fiber's `nova_current_task = &f->task` (line 3829/3941) is a gap where the task state is inconsistent. In single-carrier, this was harmless (the carrier's fault_buf was unused). With M carriers, a crash in this window kills a carrier thread, leaving all its tasks stranded (permanent deadlock for those tasks).
races.fix: Set nova_current_task BEFORE switching to the fiber (in the resume path, before SwitchToFiber/nova_asm_switch). The resume function already has `f->resumer = me` before the switch -- add `nova_current_task = &f->task` there too. The fiber entry trampoline's redundant set is fine as a safety net.

races.scenario: RACE 18: nova_rt_monitor (line 5373) checks `gt->finished` (line 5381) and then modifies `gt->monitors` array (lines 5385-5389) WITHOUT any lock. Comment says 'Single-carrier cooperative: no lock needed (only one thread).' With M carriers, carrier A calls monitor() on a task running on carrier B. Carrier B completes the task, sets finished=1, and iterates monitors[] to notify. Carrier A simultaneously modifies monitors[] to add a new entry. This is a data race on the monitors array.
races.why: The monitor registration path (realloc + append to monitors[]) and the notification path (iterate monitors[] and send to each channel, lines 4548-4549) can execute concurrently on different carriers. realloc may free and reallocate the array while the other carrier is reading it -- use-after-free. Even without realloc, the concurrent write (append) and read (iterate) is a data race.
races.fix: Add a per-task lock for monitor registration and notification, or use the NovaSchedTask's existing status field with an atomic CAS to detect the finished-vs-registering race.

races.scenario: RACE 19: channel_send_move (line 3459) has NO green-mode park path. When a green task calls send_move on a full bounded channel, it falls through to the OS-thread path which calls SleepConditionVariableCS/pthread_cond_wait (lines 3463-3464/3475-3476). This blocks the CARRIER OS thread, freezing ALL green tasks on that carrier.
races.why: nova_rt_channel_send (line 3385) has an explicit `if (nova_sched_in_task())` park loop (lines 3393-3423). But nova_rt_channel_send_move (line 3459) has NO such check -- it always takes the OS-blocking path. Under M:N, if the compiler emits send_move (for a proven-local value) and the channel is full, one carrier blocks entirely, starving potentially thousands of green tasks. This is not a data race but a functional correctness bug: the green scheduler contract (no carrier blocking) is violated.
races.fix: Add the same green-mode park loop to nova_rt_channel_send_move as exists in nova_rt_channel_send.

results.verdict: The M:N design is safe to build ONLY after all 19 issues are resolved. The critical preconditions are: (1) ALL global scheduler state (nova_sched_current, nova_sched_live, nova_sched_running, run queue, io/sleep/offload waiter lists) must become either per-carrier TLS or protected by explicit synchronization. The current runtime has at minimum 8 global variables that assume single-threaded access. (2) The fiber resume path must be made thread-migration-safe: on Windows, abandon the Fibers API in favor of asm context switch (like Go), because Windows fibers are thread-affine; on POSIX, set nova_current_task and the resumer pointer BEFORE the context switch. (3) nova_is_multithreaded must be set to 1 when M>1 carriers start, so RC operations use atomic instructions. (4) All once-init patterns must use proper atomic initialization. (5) A cross-carrier wakeup mechanism (eventfd/self-pipe) must exist to avoid 10ms latency stalls. (6) The dual scheduling architecture (global run queue + ws_deques) must be unified into a single work-stealing design. The existing ws_worker_loop (line 4713) is a DISCONNECTED prototype that does not interact with channels, I/O parking, sleep, offload, or monitors -- it would need to be rebuilt from scratch integrating all of those subsystems. Estimated scope: ~2000 lines of runtime changes affecting every scheduler path. The recommended build order is: fix nova_sched_current TLS first (unblocks everything else), then unify the run queue, then fix RC atomicity, then add carrier wakeup, then handle fiber thread-migration. Only then is it safe to spawn multiple carrier threads.
required_invariants: INV-1 (Task Identity): nova_sched_current must be __thread (TLS). Each carrier sets it to the task it is about to resume, clears it after the task yields/finishes. Enforced by: making the variable __declspec(thread) / __thread. Violation = any green task reads another carrier's current task.

INV-2 (Run Queue Exclusivity): No two carriers may concurrently mutate the same run queue without synchronization. Enforced by: per-carrier local deques with lock-free steal protocol (Chase-Lev deque), plus a locked global injection queue for cross-carrier wakes. The old nova_rq_push/pop must be deleted.

INV-3 (Fiber Thread-Affinity or Migration-Safety): A fiber must only be resumed on the OS thread that last suspended it, OR the resume path must fully rebind the fiber to the new thread (set resumer = current carrier's carrier_fiber, update nova_current_task). On Windows: do NOT use SwitchToFiber across threads; use asm context switch or UMS. Enforced by: either task-to-carrier affinity (task.home_carrier field checked on steal) or re-binding in the resume path.

INV-4 (RC Atomicity): When more than one OS thread can touch RC-managed objects (M>1 carriers), nova_is_multithreaded MUST be 1 so nova_rc_inc/dec use atomic instructions. Enforced by: setting nova_is_multithreaded = 1 in the M:N init path before starting carrier threads, not only in the OS-pool spawn path.

INV-5 (Waiter List Ownership): Each waiter list (I/O, sleep, offload) must be owned by exactly one carrier (TLS) or protected by a mutex. No carrier may iterate or mutate another carrier's waiter list without synchronization. Enforced by: making nova_io_waiters, nova_sleep_waiters, nova_offload_waiters all __thread. Park operations always add to the current carrier's local list. Poll operations always scan only the local list.

INV-6 (No Carrier Blocking): No green-mode code path may block a carrier OS thread (SleepConditionVariableCS, pthread_cond_wait, Sleep, etc.). ALL blocking operations in green tasks must park (yield to carrier) instead. Enforced by: audit every channel/socket/sleep/file path that has if(nova_sched_in_task()) branches -- currently send_move is MISSING this branch. Every new blocking API must include the green-mode park path.

INV-7 (Cross-Carrier Wakeup): When a task is made runnable (channel wake, I/O ready, offload complete, spawn) and the target carrier is blocked in select/sleep, it must be woken within O(1) time. Enforced by: a per-carrier eventfd/self-pipe included in every carrier's select() fd_set. Writers (wake paths) write a byte to the target carrier's wakeup FD.

INV-8 (Once-Init Safety): All lazy-initialized global state (slab allocator, offload pool, VEH handler, intern table, int_str_cache) must use a thread-safe once-init pattern. Enforced by: pthread_once / InitOnceExecuteOnce / atomic CAS flag with acquire/release semantics.

INV-9 (Monitor Safety): Task monitor registration and notification must be mutually exclusive. Enforced by: a per-NovaSchedTask lock (or atomic state machine) that serializes monitor[] mutations with the completion+notification path.

INV-10 (Heap Bounds Monotonicity): nova_heap_base and nova_heap_top must only ever widen (base decreases, top increases) and updates must be visible to all carriers. Enforced by: atomic CAS loops (compare-and-swap to widen) with release semantics on writes and acquire on reads in nova_rc_is_managed.

So RACE-14 (Windows fibers are thread-affine; SwitchToFiber across OS threads corrupts the TEB/SEH) is the GOVERNING constraint, not a footnote. (b) The standalone WS subsystem (ws_worker_loop @4713, nova_rt_ws_* @4756-4807) is a DISCONNECTED prototype that calls nova_rt_fiber_resume directly from worker threads â€” it already commits RACE-14 and RACE-11 and touches NONE of channels/IO/sleep/offload/monitors. It is repurposed ONLY for its deque primitives (ws_deque_init/push/pop/steal); its loop and public API are NOT the M:N path. (c) RACE-7 is real: the green spawn path (nova_rt_spawn @5304-5305) returns BEFORE the line that sets nova_is_multithreaded=1 (@5307), so green-mode RC stays non-atomic. (d) RC atomicity already has a working flag (nova_rc_inc/dec @6845-6884 branch on nova_is_multithreaded; strpool RC @318/328 too) â€” flip it ON for M>1. (e) Heap-bounds (nova_heap_base/top @168-178) and box-range (g_box_lo/hi @533-561) widen non-atomically; on x86-64 the aligned 64-bit stores are hardware-atomic, the only residual hazard is a lost-update transient NARROWING that makes nova_rc_is_managed/nova_is_box reject a valid pointer (â†’ leak, or is_box misclass). Fix = monotonic CAS-widen loops under M>1.

THE DESIGN, layer by layer (each fix tagged to the attack item it closes):

1) TASK IDENTITY (INV-1 / RACE-1). nova_sched_current (@4123) becomes __declspec(thread) on Win / __thread on POSIX. Add `static __thread int nova_carrier_id = -1;`. Each carrier sets nova_sched_current before nova_rt_fiber_resume and clears after (already the pattern @4524/4527 â€” now per-thread). nova_sched_in_task (@4140) reads the TLS copy. This single change is the keystone: every park/yield/offload/sleep reads ITS OWN carrier's current task.

2) FIBER THREAD-AFFINITY ON WINDOWS (INV-3 / RACE-5, RACE-14). This is the design's hard pivot. We do NOT adopt "Go-style free migration" on this Windows build because SwitchToFiber is thread-affine and we are NOT switching to the POSIX asm path in v1 (that is a separate, larger port). Instead: TASKS ARE PINNED TO THEIR HOME CARRIER. NovaSchedTask gains `int home_carrier;` set at creation/first-run. A parked task's wake ALWAYS re-enqueues to its HOME carrier's run-queue, never the waker's. Work-stealing (Step 3+) steals only tasks that have NEVER been resumed yet (status==0 AND home_carrier==-1, i.e. fresh fibers created but not yet run on any thread) â€” a fresh fiber has no thread affinity until its first SwitchToFiber, so the FIRST steal binds it to the stealer (set home_carrier=stealer on first resume). Once a fiber has run on carrier K, only carrier K may ever SwitchToFiber it again. This kills RACE-5 and RACE-14 by construction: no fiber is ever resumed on a thread other than the one that last suspended it. Cross-carrier wakes (RACE-5's channel case) push to the parked task's home_carrier deque + signal that carrier (INV-7). (POSIX builds CAN later enable free migration by re-binding resumer in resume â€” but that is post-v1 and gated on building the asm path on Windows; documented as the migration upgrade.)

3) RUN-QUEUE EXCLUSIVITY (INV-2 / RACE-2, RACE-12). Step 1 (first increment): keep the SINGLE global FIFO (nova_rq_head/tail) but wrap nova_rq_push/pop AND the io/sleep/offload waiter-list access in ONE global recursive-free mutex (nova_global_rq_lock). Coarse but provably correct â€” eliminates RACE-2/3/4 structural corruption at once. Step 3: replace with per-carrier deques (repurposed ws_deque, which already has a per-deque CRITICAL_SECTION) + a locked global injection queue for non-carrier spawns. The DUAL-QUEUE hazard (RACE-12 lost wakeup) is closed by RULE: there is exactly ONE scheduling fabric. All wake paths (wake_one @4176, wake_send_one @4184, wake_sleepers @4232, poll_io @4270, check_offload @4423, sched_spawn @4478) push to the SAME fabric the carrier loop pops from. In Step 1 that fabric is the global locked FIFO; in Step 3 it is the home-carrier's deque + wakeup signal. The standalone nova_rq_* and the standalone ws_worker_loop are NEVER both live.

4) WAITER-LIST OWNERSHIP (INV-5 / RACE-3, RACE-4). io_waiters/sleep_waiters/offload_waiters move from globals (@4126/4127/4331) into a per-carrier NovaCarrier struct (Step 2), single-writer = the owning carrier (the parked task ran ON that carrier, the carrier scans its own list) â€” no lock. In Step 1 they stay global but under the global mutex (correct, just coarse). park_io/park_sleep/offload_run register on g_carriers[nova_carrier_id].X.

5) NO CARRIER BLOCKING (INV-6 / RACE-19). nova_rt_channel_send_move (@3459) is MISSING the if(nova_sched_in_task()) green park loop that nova_rt_channel_send (@3393) has â€” a green task move-sending to a full bounded channel blocks the whole carrier via SleepConditionVariableCS (@3464). FIX: clone the green park loop from send into send_move. This is a correctness bug that exists even at N=2, so it is folded into Step 1.

6) RC ATOMICITY (INV-4 / RACE-7). Set nova_is_multithreaded=1 in nova_rt_main_dispatch BEFORE launching any second carrier (when computed N>1). This flips nova_rc_inc/dec (@6853/6872) and strpool RC (@318/328) to interlocked. Folded into Step 1.

7) HEAP-BOUNDS + BOX-RANGE MONOTONICITY (INV-10 / RACE-9, RACE-10, RACE-15). Under M>1, nova_track_heap_bounds (@175) and nova_box_track (@536) use a CAS-widen loop (InterlockedCompareExchange64 on Win) so the range only ever widens and a lost update can never transiently narrow it. Reads in nova_rc_is_managed/nova_is_box use plain aligned loads (atomic on x86-64). On this Windows/x86-64 target these are aligned 8-byte stores, so the practical risk is only the lost-widen; the CAS loop removes it. Folded into Step 1 as a 6-line guarded change (only compiled-in when carriers>1, so single-carrier hot path is untouched â€” protects GATE 4/5).

8) ONCE-INIT SAFETY (INV-8 / RACE-16). nova_offload_ensure (@4369) and nova_slab_init use a plain flag check+set. Guard each with InitOnceExecuteOnce (Win) so two carriers starting simultaneously can't double-init the offload pool / slab pages. nova_install_fiber_veh (@3820) is already idempotent-enough (AddVectoredExceptionHandler twice is benign) but also gets the once-guard.

9) MONITOR SAFETY (INV-9 / RACE-18). nova_rt_monitor mutates gt->monitors[] and the completion path (@4548-4549) iterates it. Because tasks are HOME-CARRIER-PINNED and a task's completion runs on its home carrier, the only cross-thread case is monitor() called from a DIFFERENT carrier's task. Add a per-task lock (CRITICAL_SECTION) taken around both monitor registration and the notify loop. Folded into Step 2 (when waiter lists go per-carrier, monitors cross carriers).

10) CROSS-CARRIER WAKEUP (INV-7 / RACE-13). Step 2+: each carrier gets a wakeup primitive (Win: a per-carrier auto-reset Event added to the idle wait; the carrier's idle path waits with timeout on its Event instead of bare Sleep(1)). Any wake/spawn/offload-completion targeting carrier K sets K's Event. Step 1 keeps the existing Sleep(1)/10ms-select idle with a 1ms cap so latency is bounded (<=1ms) without new machinery â€” acceptable for the first correct increment; the Event upgrade is Step 6.

11) FAULT BOUNDARY (RACE-17). In nova_rt_fiber_resume set nova_current_task=&f->task BEFORE SwitchToFiber/asm_switch (currently only the fiber entry trampoline sets it). With pinning this window is single-thread per fiber so the existing code is already safe, but the pre-set is a cheap belt-and-suspenders folded into Step 1's resume edit.

NET: the design is "pinned-fiber M:N" â€” Go's GMP topology (per-carrier deques + global fallback + steal) but with Windows-fiber thread-affinity preserved via home-carrier pinning instead of free goroutine migration. Every one of the 19 attacks maps to a concrete fix above; none is deferred without an explicit gating reason (free migration, lock-free Chase-Lev, Event-driven idle are the three legitimately-post-v1 OPTIMIZATIONS, all correctness-neutral).

synth.race_validation:
TSan is effectively unavailable on this clang/Windows/CreateFiber setup (fiber stack switches defeat TSan's happens-before shadow; ThreadSanitizer on Windows-MSVC-ABI clang is not reliably supported). So validation is INVARIANT-DRIVEN STRESS, not sanitizer-driven, with four legs:

(1) THE EXISTING SUITE UNDER NOVA_CARRIERS=N. _run_regression_gen4.ps1 â†’ _run_final_regression.ps1 already pre-compiles output/nova_runtime.c once, runs ~400 tests in parallel with KILL-ON-TIMEOUT (15s run cap, _proc_util.ps1 Invoke-Timed â€” mandatory per the safety memo; WaitForExit does NOT kill). Run the whole suite at NOVA_CARRIERS=1,2,4,8 and assert the PASS count is IDENTICAL at every N. The 6 concurrency tests (async_test, select_test, select_multi_test, yield_test, parallel_test, bounded_chan_test) plus green_transparent/green_monitor_test/green_supervisor_test/green_netpoll_test/green_scale_test are the concurrency core. A race that corrupts the run-queue or RC will surface as a non-deterministic FAIL/crash/timeout that appears at N>=2 but not N=1 â€” the differential across N IS the race detector.

(2) STRESS HARNESS (many carriers x many tasks x channels x spawn-storms, REPEATED). A new _race_stress.ps1 that, for reps in 1..200, builds+runs a green program: P producers each spawning S tasks (P*S = 50k) that fan-in to one channel, plus a phase where 10k tasks each PARK on a private channel then are woken (the green_scale_test phase-2 GenServer pattern â€” the hardest park/unpark cross-carrier case), plus a nested spawn-storm (each task spawns 10 subtasks). The program asserts EXACT conservation: total_received == total_sent, sum == closed-form expected (n + n*(n-1)/2 as green_scale_test already does @53). Run at NOVA_CARRIERS=cpu_count. Any lost wakeup (RACE-12/13), double-run (RACE-2 pop), or corrupted identity (RACE-1) breaks conservation â†’ assert fires non-zero exit â†’ harness records the rep seed. 200 reps x multiple N is the probabilistic coverage that replaces TSan. Each rep is individually kill-on-timeout wrapped.

(3) INVARIANT ASSERTS COMPILED INTO THE RUNTIME (NOVA_SCHED_DEBUG build). Guarded by #ifdef NOVA_SCHED_DEBUG so zero cost in release (protects GATE 4/5): (a) on resume, assert task->status==0 and (if bound) task->home_carrier==nova_carrier_id â€” catches a fiber being resumed on the wrong thread (RACE-5/14) and double-resume (RACE-2). (b) a global atomic g_running_count incremented before resume / decremented after; assert it never exceeds g_carrier_count â€” catches two carriers running the same fiber. (c) park_committed monotonic 0â†’1, assert wake never reads 0 after spin â€” catches the F1 window (RACE-1/5 park/wake overlap). (d) on task free, assert status==3 â€” catches use-after-free of a still-queued task. Build the stress harness binaries with -DNOVA_SCHED_DEBUG so the asserts are live during validation; ship release without.

(4) CARRIER-ATTRIBUTION + CONSERVATION STAMP. Each NovaSchedTask records the carrier_id that completes it; green_scale_test (and the stress harness) print the distinct-carrier-id set and the completion count. PASS requires BOTH: distinct ids >= 2 (proves genuine multi-thread, not accidental single-carrier fallback) AND completions == spawned (proves no leak/loss). This converts the existing scale test into a race oracle for free.

Backstop where a sanitizer IS reachable: on any WSL/Linux POSIX checkout (the asm-switch path), run the stress harness under clang -fsanitize=thread; on Windows, run the release stress binary under Application Verifier (heap + locks) to catch the heap-bounds/box-range and double-free classes (RACE-9/10/15/18). These are opportunistic, not the primary gate â€” the primary gate is the differential-across-N suite + conservation stress + debug invariants.
